answer: Endorsement travels across a cut in the endorsement graph, and a cut is only real when the two sides have no common ancestor inside the endorsement horizon, so a cluster must be dissolved and rebuilt before its weight counts elsewhere. This cost is per identity, so it cannot be amortised across the fleet. The prism is the island, the opal the endorsement that crosses it, and the voyage the shared ancestor that would disqualify the crossing; one prism is cheap to hold, but an opal only counts when no voyage exists, and that takes independent history.
